---
title: "Cross-calibration"
---

## When to use it

Use `fit_cross_calibrator()` when your treatment-effect model was trained with cross-fitting. Fit the calibration map using pooled out-of-fold predictions, then apply it to predictions from every fold-specific model. This uses the full sample without a separate calibration split.

For each fold, train the treatment-effect model without that fold's observations. Save its predictions for all observations, not only its held-out fold.

## Prepare the inputs

| Input | Shape | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `predictions` | Length `n` | One out-of-fold prediction per observation, used to fit the map |
| `fold_predictions` | `n × K` | Column `k` contains predictions from the model trained without fold `k` |
| `fold_ids` | Length `n`, optional | Indices `1` through `K` identifying the held-out fold for each observation |
| Treatment, outcome, and nuisance estimates | Length `n` each | Inputs required by the chosen loss |

Supply `fold_ids` to check that each pooled prediction equals the entry in its designated column of `fold_predictions`.

## Fit and predict

::: {.panel-tabset}
### Python

```python
from causal_calibration import fit_cross_calibrator, validate_crossfit_bundle

validate_crossfit_bundle(
    predictions=tau_oof,
    fold_predictions=tau_fold_matrix,
    fold_ids=fold_ids,
)

cross_calibrator = fit_cross_calibrator(
    predictions=tau_oof,
    fold_predictions=tau_fold_matrix,
    fold_ids=fold_ids,
    treatment=a,
    outcome=y,
    mu0=mu0_hat,
    mu1=mu1_hat,
    propensity=e_hat,
    loss="dr",
    method="isotonic",
)

tau_cross_calibrated = cross_calibrator.predict(tau_fold_matrix)
```

### R

```r
library(causalCalibration)

validate_crossfit_bundle(
  predictions = tau_oof,
  fold_predictions = tau_fold_matrix,
  fold_ids = fold_ids
)

cross_calibrator <- fit_cross_calibrator(
  predictions = tau_oof,
  fold_predictions = tau_fold_matrix,
  fold_ids = fold_ids,
  treatment = a,
  outcome = y,
  mu0 = mu0_hat,
  mu1 = mu1_hat,
  propensity = e_hat,
  loss = "dr",
  method = "isotonic"
)

tau_cross_calibrated <- predict(cross_calibrator, tau_fold_matrix)
```

:::

## Combine predictions

The package fits one map on the pooled out-of-fold scores, applies it to each column of `fold_predictions`, and takes the median in each row. For an even number of columns, it uses the lower of the two middle values.

For predictions on the training observations, supply the original `n × K` matrix. For a new sample of size `m`, apply each fold-specific treatment-effect model to the new observations and supply the resulting `m × K` matrix, keeping the same column order.

## Common mistakes

- Using fitted in-sample scores in `predictions` instead of out-of-fold scores.
- Passing a vector to `predict()` instead of the full matrix of fold-specific predictions.
- Changing the column order between fitting and prediction.
- Omitting `fold_ids` when you want the package to check out-of-fold alignment.
